external_relations.target_title: security: audit mutable extension sources and legacy npm identity aliases

source.description:
## PROBLEM

Native dispatch resolves sources ONCE to strings, then loads the bytes more than once:
1. a fenced builtin-baseline session (no extensions),
2. a fenced discovery session over the dynamic sources (getActiveToolNames -> the pinned names),
3. the real child session (curated + dynamic), created with tools = the finalised allowlist.
Post-load verification is NAME-only (missingPromisedTools compares getActiveToolNames() sets).

Measured by the SPECIALISTS-85 read-only audit: nothing anywhere in the path hashes, snapshots, or
re-attests bytes. A source that mutates between step 2 and step 3 -- npm reinstall, git pull, in-place
body edit, symlink swap, or an extension that rewrites itself -- executes DIFFERENT code under an
IDENTICAL name set, while the prompt contract, activation_admitted.tools, the forensic pinned list and
the tools allowlist all describe the pre-mutation registry. The cheapest attacker action (edit a
function body, rename nothing) is exactly the action no gate detects.

Evidence: src/activation/native-host.ts discovery load vs real load; name-only post-load recheck;
withDiscoveredToolContract appends names only; legacy policy extension matches by name too. Full
report and file:line list in SPECIALISTS-85.

## SEVERITY - STATED HONESTLY

This is an INTEGRITY/AUDITABILITY gap, NOT a privilege escalation. The operator enabled the source,
and extension registration code already runs at load, so M1 grants nothing they did not authorise.
What is lost is the ability to answer "which bytes ran?" from the activation record, and the guarantee
that the contract the operator approved describes the code that executed. Not release-blocking; fixable
in a bounded change.

## WHAT IS ALREADY CORRECT (do not regress)

All four refusals fail closed when they fire: collision, provenance, shadow, mixed-baseline; the
empty-discovery throw; and post-load tool_contract_unsatisfied. A mutation that REMOVES a pinned name,
or ADDS a colliding/shadowing name after discovery, IS caught. The exposure is strictly same-set code
swap.

## FIX DIRECTION

Bind attestation to bytes, not more name checks: take content identity at discovery (hash or git
commit for git: checkouts, resolved-package hash for npm:, file mtime+hash for local paths), re-verify
it before prompt render and before EVERY session creation (primary, fallback, retry, resume), and record
it in activation_admitted/snapshot. Any mismatch refuses rather than proceeding.

## SMALLER FINDINGS FROM THE SAME AUDIT (carry with the fix, do not lose)

- A1: npm:/local tools are pooled in ONE discovery session, so provenance is class-level, not
  source-level; the record cannot say which enabled source contributed which tool. Needs per-source
  discovery or a per-tool source->declared-spec map.
- A2 (not-verifiable here): whether pi's sourceInfo.source derives from the load path or from package
  metadata lives in the pi SDK, outside this repo. If a package can influence its own label, provenance
  is spoofable. Unverified, not a defect.
- I1: the npm @spec is decorative at load time - version is ignored on purpose, affects only the
  collision key, so an installed dir can drift from a reviewed spec with no enforcement or warning.
- I2 (unproven): no npm-alias normalisation was found; 'name equality == code equality' would break if
  aliases appear. Not verified against pi's install semantics.
- M2: curated-vs-discovery pool divergence remains the accepted gap (residual 2) with its expiry trigger;
  unchanged by this audit.
- M3: fallback/retry reuse the same allowlist and loader against live bytes; resume() re-verifies nothing.
- Boundary invisibility: no hash/commit/version and no load cost is recorded anywhere operator-visible;
  skipped sources are stderr-only warnings.
- Known and pre-existing: extension code mutating through its own exec path bypasses the lease/tool gate
  (the gate covers the LLM tool path only).
source.notes:
CLOSEOUT (true closeout of the unitAI-1pqtl extension-resolution window, verified at master 4dbc2261; receipt published in .xtrm/reports/2026-09-16-unitAI-1pqtl-extension-tools.md section 'True closeout').

STILL OPEN, CORRECTLY SCOPED, NOT SUPERSEDED. Re-read against current master: post-load verification is still name-only (src/activation/native-host.ts createVerifiedSession -> missingPromisedTools compares getActiveToolNames sets), and the discovery load remains a separate load from the real child session, so same-name-set code substitution is still silently accepted. Nothing landed between the SPECIALISTS-85 audit and this closeout that satisfies the fix direction.

CLASSIFICATION CONFIRMED: integrity/auditability gap, NOT privilege escalation, and NOT a release blocker. All four refusals still fail closed when they fire; empty discovery still refuses; post-load tool_contract_unsatisfied still refuses; a mutation that removes a pinned name or adds a colliding/shadowing one is still caught.

CLOSURE CONDITION unchanged: bind attestation to bytes (content identity at discovery; re-verify before prompt render and before every session creation; record in activation_admitted/snapshot; refuse on mismatch), carrying the smaller findings A1 (per-source attribution), I1 (npm @spec decorative at load) and M3 (resume re-verifies nothing).

This closeout explicitly did NOT close this by implication from the parent epic unitAI-1pqtl being closed.
